outcome: LOADED AND VERIFIED; STAGE STOPPED BEFORE INDEXNOW
stopReason: Step 3 cannot be performed as specified: npm run discovery:indexnow submits the legacy publication set, not this tier's indexable set, and would announce 756 URLs the sitemap deliberately withholds. Nothing was submitted. Step 4 was still run because it is read-only; it found a structured-data regression on all 610 pages and 93 indexed records at four clicks. Tier 2 was not started.

load.target: Railway RNAwiki / production PostgreSQL over the Railway TCP proxy, sslmode verify-ca, PGSSLSERVERNAME=localhost
load.checkpoints: state.json phase 5 step materialise-tier-1, batches 1-7, recorded by the loader's own batch.ts calls
load.staleMarkerNote: Two markers from a 2026-09-04 smoke load (threshold 3, disposable database) were present. Their input digests no longer matched the Phase 5a corpus, so the dry run reported 0 skipped and every batch was rebuilt against production. No batch was skipped on the strength of a pre-production marker.

loaderChange.why: The deployment plan (step 2) states the loader 'takes an explicit production URL and refuses without --production-confirmed'. No such guard existed: the flag was accepted and ignored, so any remote DATABASE_URL loaded production without a confirmation step.
loaderChange.change: A non-dry-run write to a host that is neither localhost nor *.railway.internal now throws unless --production-confirmed is passed. The existing working-database guard is unchanged.
loaderChange.verified: Refusal reproduced against the production URL without the flag; typecheck clean; the load then ran with the flag.

indexNow.command: npm run discovery:indexnow -- --origin https://rnawiki.com (dry run only)
indexNow.blocker: scripts/discovery/submit-indexnow.ts builds its URL set from loadMedicineSitemapIndexabilityReports(), the legacy publication projection. It has no corpus or tier awareness and no --tier flag.
indexNow.invariantBroken: The script's own contract - 'it can never announce a URL the sitemap withholds' - stopped holding the moment corpus_pages became the sitemap's authority for a corpus slug. 756 Tier 1 pages held back below the threshold of 11 present fields would have been announced to IndexNow.
indexNow.decision: Not submitted. Announcing 756 deliberately withheld URLs is a worse outcome than a delayed submission, and the fix changes what the whole site announces, so it belongs to the spec owner rather than to this stage.

clickDepth.requirement: 0 (R12: every indexed record within three clicks of home)
clickDepth.firstRunNote: The default 600-page budget was exhausted on the first run, which the script itself says makes a deep record untrustworthy. The recorded figures are from the re-run with a 5000-page budget, which finished the walk in 729 pages.

cause.method: Independent breadth-first walk from home to depth 4 recording the first page that links each record (93 of 93 located).
cause.explanation: 68 records are first linked from a letter sub-page of a facet value that splits by letter (home -> facet index -> facet value -> letter sub-page -> record). 25 are first linked from page 2 or later of a facet value that paginates without splitting (home -> facet index -> facet value -> ?page=n -> record). Both are the structure docs/specs/browse.md describes; neither is a browse or facet defect, so nothing was changed. What is new is the population: Tier 1 gives pathway and class values enough records that these two shapes now carry 15% of the tier's indexed records instead of a rare few.
cause.wouldNeedASpecChange: Putting these 93 within three clicks means linking letter sub-pages or later pages from the facet index itself, which changes docs/specs/browse.md.

discoveryState.cause: app/d/[slug]/page.tsx returns the corpus branch (CorpusDossierPage) before reaching the legacy branch's <script type="application/ld+json"> block, so no corpus page emits structured data. A legacy dossier still serves 2 ld+json blocks; every one of the 610 Tier 1 pages serves 0.
discoveryState.effect: Every page this tier promoted lost the structured data it had as a legacy page. The monitor therefore records DISCOVERY_READY for none of them.
discoveryState.notFixedHere: The fix is a code change to the deployed dossier route and needs its own build, gate and deployment, which is not this stage.

issues: IndexNow submission is not corpus-aware: it would announce 756 URLs the sitemap withholds and would miss 45 of this tier's 610 indexable URLs. Nothing was submitted.
Structured-data regression: all 610 Tier 1 pages serve no application/ld+json, where their legacy versions served two. Cause located in app/d/[slug]/page.tsx.
93 of 610 indexed Tier 1 records are four clicks from home, against R12's three. Caused by the designed letter-split and pagination paths meeting a larger population, not by a browse defect.
scripts/corpus-20k/load/materialise.ts had no --production-confirmed guard despite the deployment plan stating it does. Added and verified before the load.
npm run discovery:monitor runs out of heap when it follows the full sitemap index (8926 records; OOM after 4823 under Node's default heap). It completed for this tier when scoped to tier-1.xml.
